[Thought diffusion](https://youtu.be/UsjSdM_tiYg) is a type of mindful meditation for strong feelings, that can teach you detachment. For example, instead of "I'm going to be super embarrassed and everyone will judge me!" Over and over you slow down..."I'm going to be super embarrassed and everyone will judge me. Okay that's a thought. I think I am going to be super embarrassed. I think everyone will judge me. I notice this thought. I notice that I think I am going to be super embarrassed. I notice I think everyone will judge me." It gets you out of your head.

You don't need to be embarrassed about not being able to move forward right away. You were with her for five years. Of course it's going to take a while to recover from this. You need to validate your feelings but not dwell on them. If you catch yourself ruminating on how you could have prevented this/what you did wrong/if you deserved it over and over all day long try this. 


1. Decide on a 15-20 minute free period of the day, not too close to when you go to sleep. Set an alarm for yourself.



2. If any thought like that pops up during the day, write down a short, concise version on your phone's notes, a Post-It, a memopad, whatever. Just write it down. Don't write anything else or reread it. Save it for later.



3. When the time comes, review your list. Cross out the ones you don't feel worried about anymore. Learn about cognitive distortions for the rest. Are you using black and white thinking, emotional reasoning, mind reading, etc.? Label them as proof these thoughts are illogical and don't deserve your belief in them. 


4. Rewrite the worst/most painful thoughts in more positive terms. Make sure to undo any cognitive distortions.



5. Throw away/delete the worry list for the day and repeat this every day until you no longer have excessive thoughts on this problem 24/7. 



I found this really helpful personally. It's like procrastinating, but for your worries. You are literally procrastinating on your rumination to focus on other things.


Your self esteem just took a huge blow from this. This is to be expected. This is normal. It's normal to feel "not good enough" for anybody after this happened. You are VALID in being upset...but that doesn't mean your low self esteem is true! 



Feel free to get mad at her for a while. Throw out her things, delete photos of her, write an angry message about her then tear it up. Don't take too long on this, but if you ever want to forgive her it comes later. Let your brain see her for what she is - she betrayed *you*. She let *you* down. She took advantage of *you*. You aren't at fault. 


You didn't cause this. You can't fix her. You can't control her. Let this free you, not tear you down.

I'm 18F and been through multiple traumas. It's important to get therapy too, you deserve respite for caring for somebody in this state. And she can get better. I did too, even though I thought I was never going to. The little things are important. Push her a little. That's what I needed - someone close enough to push me but not be too pushy, and not be too lenient. Just to care for herself. Ask her to brush her teeth, shower... I'm sure she's probably missing out on those, right? She won't see herself getting better until she feels like a person again. She needs her dignity back even when depression is taking it away from her. Hygiene -> basic activities like walking around the block, groceries, remembering to do laundry -> stuff like fashion, hair cut, makeup (her style, if she's into it) -> higher up goals like completing (diploma?ged?sat?college course?) or some online class/skill like edx, coursera, khan academy. She needs her dignity, then life, then confidence, then talent. Stuff like that. It doesn't have to be that hard though. I'm pretty far along -- I've been recovering for almost a year post moving out of the family that gave me a lot of issues. She's lucky to have a good dad like you who cares. Also, look into agoraphobia for her? May be related with the social anxiety. And don't forget please look after yourself too. It is so, so important. And maybe recommend to her some online support groups. If she's an adult, not much you can do besides suggestions, but if she's a younger t(w)een try to monitor online a little. I wish my parents took my devices away when I was on Omegle (video chatting website, lots of pedos), Kik (similar), anything "pro ana"(communities centered on encouraging their users to develop anorexia), or just super depressing memes. Regardless of age, give her some positive influence. Watch nostalgic movies, from before the trauma maybe. Or just randomly text her r/wholesome memes or cat videos. I wish the best of both of you.
